svg.title: Three-short-blast distress signal
svg.desc: A product-neutral Australian distress-signal card. Use it only when safe and useful and when searchers may be nearby. Give three distinct short whistle blasts, stop and listen, then repeat at intervals only if safe. No seconds, distance, sound level or reply code is supplied because sources conflict and conditions control detection. Do not exhaust an injured or breathless person, blow near another person's ear, or delay first aid, shelter, emergency communication, satellite SOS or PLB use. Hearing or seeing a response does not prove that rescuers have identified the person or that rescue is coming. The subjective wording-confidence estimates are 90 percent for the three-signal core and 65 percent for completeness.
svg.text: Whistle distress signal: three short blasts
WARNING — A SIGNAL IS NOT CONFIRMED CONTACT
Use this pattern only when it is safe and useful.
Subjective wording-confidence estimate: 90% for the three-signal
core; 65% for timing, repetition and hearing-safety completeness.
These rate the wording—not whether anyone hears you or rescue follows.
No seconds, detection distance, sound level or reply code is supplied.
Victorian SAR, hearing-safety and stressed-reader review is outstanding.
1 CHECK THAT WHISTLING IS SAFE AND USEFUL
• Use it when searchers or other helpers may be nearby.
• Keep first aid, shelter and emergency communication going.
• Do not force an injured, breathless or exhausted person to blow.
If it is unsafe or impossible, stop and use another safe signal.
2 GIVE THREE DISTINCT SHORT BLASTS
SHORT BLAST
SHORT BLAST
SHORT BLAST
Keep the three blasts clearly separate.
Do not add an invented duration or range.
3 STOP WHISTLING AND LISTEN
• Listen for voices, whistles and direct instructions.
• Look without leaving the safe waiting place.
• Preserve breath, warmth, attention and communication power.
Do not treat a possible reply as confirmation that you were found.
4 REPEAT AT INTERVALS — ONLY IF SAFE
• Repeat the same three distinct short blasts.
• Pause and listen after each group.
• Return to first aid, shelter, warmth and communication tasks.
Do not whistle continuously or exhaust yourself.
TERMINAL CAUTIONS
• Never blow close to another person's ear.
• No response does not prove the signal failed.
• A response does not prove rescuers identified you.
• Continue the rescue plan until direct responder instructions.
This card does not replace 000, satellite SOS, a PLB or Chapter 3.
Basis: current February 2026 NATSAR Manual S-240 and EP-013
WORKING DRAFT — NOT FIELD-APPROVED
